comments.body:
=== THE REQUIRED LIVE-PATH EXPERIMENT HAS NOW BEEN RUN. RESULT: PREDICTED-TRUE. ===

Run before any code change, as this ticket's acceptance criteria demand. Local only; no live
Jira. Harness: the faithful acli stub in
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_once.py` (`_make_acli_module`), driving
the REAL `reconcile.reconcile_once` in LIVE (persist) mode, with `create_issue` wrapped to record
every call.

  Pass 1: working set = [DIG-9]  -> primes prev_snapshot with DIG-9.
  Pass 2: working set = []       -> DIG-9 present in prev, absent from curr.

OBSERVED on pass 2:

  pass2 mutation_count = 1
  create_issue calls    = 1
  payload = {'summary': 'a bound issue that will be deleted',
             'title':   'a bound issue that will be deleted',
             'ticket_type': 'Task', 'status': {'name': 'To Do'}}

The fields are derived from the STALE PREV summary, exactly as predicted. No downstream guard
drops it: `_cross_project_targets` skips `action == "create"` outright, and `create_one`'s JQL
dedup degenerates because `EXCLUDED_FIELDS` strips `local_id` from the payload. The issue is
RESURRECTED. This ticket is a defect, not a not-a-defect.

Differ-boundary reproduction (no orchestrator at all), also run:

  differ.compute_mutations({'RBJWUOX-1': <snapshot entry>}, {})
  -> outbound create RBJWUOX-1
     provenance={'source':'differ','reason':'unbound_local','local_id':'RBJWUOX-1'}

Note `local_id == target` (the Jira key), the `_derive_provenance` fallback, byte-for-byte the
harness-30724309686 signature this ticket recorded.

=== SAME ROOT CAUSE AS 727f, DIFFERENT EMISSION ARM ===

`run_differs.py:222` passes `(prev_snapshot, curr_snapshot)` — two REMOTE fetches — into
`compute_mutations(local_state, jira_state)`. Confirmed by reading `reconcile.py:269-286`:
`prev_snapshot` is the persisted earlier FETCH and `curr_snapshot` is a fresh FETCH. Neither
reads `local_tickets`. So at this one call site the `local_state` parameter is not local state,
and `compute_mutations`'s three per-key arms divide cleanly:

  * key in local_state only  -> `_compute_mutations_emit_local_only` -> outbound create
    (`unbound_local`). Here that means "in prev, gone from curr" = deleted OR merely aged out of
    the fetch window. Emitting a create RESURRECTS it. WRONG. <- THIS TICKET.
  * key in jira_state only   -> `_compute_mutations_emit_jira_only` -> inbound create
    (`jira_new`). Here that means a genuinely new remote issue. CORRECT — the snapshot differ's
    one real job at this call site.
  * key in both              -> `_compute_mutations_emit_both` -> outbound update
    (`field_drift`) carrying the stale prev value. WRONG. <- ticket 727f.

So 727f's fix does NOT cover this: it filters `reason="field_drift"` outbound UPDATEs only, and
this is a `reason="unbound_local"` outbound CREATE. Verified by re-running the differ-boundary
reproduction with 727f's suppression applied — the create still emits. The two tickets are one
mechanism with two observables, and both are fixed at the same call site by the same rule: at
`run_differs.py:222`, drop the emissions whose correctness depends on `local_state` genuinely
being local state.

CITED AUTHORITY that this is a defect: ADR 0028 Decision para 1 — "No destructive or terminal
action ... may be driven by a key's absence from the fetched snapshot." A resurrect-create is a
terminal action so driven. Corroborating precedent at HEAD (ae009443a9, ticket b9b8), which
reworked `test_a_deleted_dc_issue_is_planned_as_an_inbound_probe` for the same reason: the probe
loop "reads a `jira_key` field that a Jira snapshot entry does not carry, and its only caller
passes the previous snapshot."

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== FIXED, RED-FIRST, IN THE SAME CHANGE AS 727f. ===

The 727f fix did NOT already cover this — verified, not assumed. That suppression matched only
`(outbound, update, field_drift)`; this defect is `(outbound, create, unbound_local)`, and the
resurrect-create still emitted with it applied. So the suppression was generalised rather than
reused: `reconcile_helpers.drop_snapshot_echo_field_updates` becomes
`drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions`, matching a `(direction, action, reason)` triple set

    ("outbound", "update", "field_drift")    <- 727f
    ("outbound", "create", "unbound_local")  <- this ticket

plus a mandatory `provenance["source"] == "differ"` conjunct so invariant-seeded mutations that
reuse a reason string are never swept up. `differ.compute_mutations` is unmodified.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

1. "The experiment above is run and recorded before any code change." DONE — see the previous
   comment. Result PREDICTED-TRUE: `client.create_issue` called once on pass 2 with fields
   rebuilt from the stale prev summary.
2. "A key absent from the current snapshot but present in the previous one never reaches
   `create_issue`, proven by a RED-first unit test." DONE, at two boundaries:
   * `orchestrate/test_reconcile_once.py::test_a_key_absent_from_the_current_snapshot_never_reaches_create_issue`
     — the live-path oracle, asserting at the TRANSPORT (`create_issue` recorded, must be never
     called) precisely because both downstream guards were shown not to catch it.
   * `diffing/test_snapshot_differ_stale_local_state.py::test_a_key_that_left_the_fetch_window_plans_no_outbound_create`
     — the diff-phase oracle, with a fixture precondition asserting the raw differ really does
     emit the `unbound_local` create so the cell cannot pass vacuously.
   Both seen RED against origin/main with a failure message naming the mechanism, GREEN after.
3. "`differ.py:7-11` and `run_differs.py:205` are corrected so the module docstring stops
   describing a contract the caller does not honour." DONE. `differ.py`'s module docstring now
   carries a CAVEAT naming the unmigrated caller, which arms misfire there, and where the
   compensation lives; `run_differs`'s docstring says the same from the caller's side. Both state
   that migrating the caller and deleting the suppression must happen in the SAME change.

MUTATION CHECK: removing `("outbound","create","unbound_local")` from the suppressed set returns
exactly this ticket's two oracles to RED with the resurrect message, while both 727f oracles stay
GREEN — so the suppression is correctly scoped per arm, and each ticket's oracle really pins its
own arm. No AttributeError / import-error style false mutation.

COMPLETENESS: fed a realistic fetched-snapshot pair, `compute_mutations` can emit exactly three
things — `jira_new` inbound create (correct here, preserved), `unbound_local` outbound create and
`field_drift` outbound update (both suppressed). This ticket's observation that the remaining
local_state-shaped arms are inert is CONFIRMED: `duplicate_local_id`, `ambiguous_local_binding`,
`dangling_jira_local_id` and `_compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes` never fire from a
fetched snapshot, because they read `local_id` / `jira_key` fields such an entry never carries.
So no residual wrong emission is left at this call site.

STILL OPEN, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE — the section of this ticket headed "the differ's
local_state contract was never migrated" describes a larger latent problem this change only
DOCUMENTS: the `(inbound, probe)` dispatch chain (`run_differs`, `inbound_probe.py`,
`backend.probe_remote`) still has no live producer, because its only producer is the unreachable
absent-partner loop. That is a missing capability, not this defect, and ADR 0028 para 2's
direct-GET confirmation path is where a deleted issue should actually be resolved. Worth its own
ticket rather than smuggling a new subsystem into a bug fix.

GATES: `make lint` clean, `make typecheck` clean, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` 1808 passed.

compiled_state.description:
# A bound key that leaves the fetch window is planned as an outbound CREATE, resurrecting it

## Status

DISCOVERED, NOT FIXED. Surfaced while triaging J11's inbound-probe cell
(`5200-e04e-246e-4aae`). The static chain is complete but the live-path confirmation
experiment has NOT been run, so this is filed for its own RED-first investigation rather
than patched blind. Confidence ~0.7.

## What was observed

Deleting a bound DC issue and running a scoped DRY-RUN produced exactly one plan entry for
the pair, quoted from harness run 30724309686:

    {'direction': 'outbound', 'action': 'create', 'target': 'RBJWUOX-1', 'local_id': 'RBJWUOX-1'}

An outbound CREATE, targeted at the Jira key of the issue that was just deleted, built from
the STALE previous snapshot. Reproduced with no Jira at all by calling
`differ.compute_mutations({'RBJWUOX-1': <snapshot entry>}, {})`, which emits that entry
byte-for-byte including the `local_id == target` fallback (`differ.py:121-131`).

## Mechanism

`run_differs.py:222` calls `compute_mutations(ctx.prev_snapshot, ctx.curr_snapshot, ...)`, so
the parameter named `local_state` is in fact the PREVIOUS JIRA SNAPSHOT. A key present in
prev and absent from curr therefore takes the "local only" arm and emits an outbound create
(`differ.py:421-441`). The dd-4 short-circuit that would suppress it (`differ.py:377-380`)
cannot fire, because `bound_local_ids` is built from a `local_id` field that a fetched
snapshot entry never carries (`differ.py:213-224` vs `fetcher.py:479` and the contract shape
at `_snapshot_schema.py:96-135`).

Downstream, two guards fail to catch it:

- `applier.py:253-278` (`_cross_project_targets`) skips `action == "create"` entirely, on the
  stated assumption that a create's key is a local-id placeholder — false here, it is a real
  Jira key.
- `create_one`'s JQL dedup keys on `mutation["local_id"]`, which is empty because
  `EXCLUDED_FIELDS` strips `local_id` from the payload (`config.py:5`), degenerating the query
  to `labels = "rebar-id:"` (`dispatch_one.py:236-256`).

`apply_planning.py:62-63` even prioritises outbound creates into the cap window.

## Why this matters beyond hard deletes

The same trigger fires for any key that merely AGES OUT of the fetch window — a
`status = Done` issue beyond `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` — not only for a deleted one. That makes this
a violation of ADR 0028 Decision §1: "no destructive or terminal action may be driven by a
key's absence from the fetched snapshot." A resurrect-create is as much a terminal action as
a retire.

Vendor-neutral code throughout, so Cloud is affected identically.

## Also recorded: the differ's local_state contract was never migrated

`differ.py:7-11` states that this module REPLACED the legacy
`compute_mutations(prev_snapshot, next_snapshot)` contract with
`compute_mutations(local_state, jira_state)`. Its sole production caller
(`run_differs.py:222`) was never migrated. Every local_state-shaped feature is therefore
inert: `bound_local_ids` always empty, the duplicate-local-id and ambiguous-local-binding arms
never fire, `_derive_provenance` always falls back to `local_id = target`, and
`_compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes` (`differ.py:610-650`) is unreachable — which
also makes the entire `(inbound, probe)` dispatch chain (`run_differs.py:349-395`,
`inbound_probe.py`, `backend.probe_remote`) a documented subsystem with no live producer. The
only fixture that supplies a `jira_key`-bearing `local_state` is
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py:38-39`.

## The experiment that must run first

Fake-client `reconcile_once` in LIVE mode (harness:
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_once.py`) with
`prev_snapshot = {"DIG-9": {...}}`, `curr_snapshot = {}`, an in-project target so
`_cross_project_targets` cannot mask the result, and a recording fake client.

- Predicted TRUE: `client.create_issue` is called once, with fields derived from the stale
  prev summary.
- Predicted FALSE: no create call, meaning a guard not yet found drops it, and this ticket
  closes as not-a-defect.

Repeat with an out-of-project key to show the guard's create exemption.

## Acceptance criteria

- The experiment above is run and recorded on this ticket before any code change.
- If TRUE: a key absent from the current snapshot but present in the previous one never
  reaches `create_issue`, proven by a RED-first unit test at the differ or applier boundary.
- Whichever way it resolves, `differ.py:7-11` and `run_differs.py:205` are corrected so the
  module docstring stops describing a contract the caller does not honour.
compiled_state.title: snapshot-absent key planned as an outbound create
